decisions.summary: The change computation moves to triage/change.rs; blocks are paired old with new (exact matches dropped, then tool clears, then difflib ratio >= 0.6, PAIR_RATIO taken from the blind test).
decisions.why: Mechanism for the approved first filter and paired-block triage; it decides how to do what was asked, not what is reviewed.

decisions.summary: A block whose claim words, after removing footnote markers and markup (comments, tags, links, glossary marks already gone), are unchanged or empty is cleared by the tool.
decisions.why: This is the GM's own split, verbatim in request.md: 'straightforward adjustments that never could have plausibly needed this kind of cascade', and his approved rule 'only a claim-changing edit triggers review'. An edit that leaves no claim word changed is exactly that case.

decisions.summary: An original-language quotation is NOT taken out of claim words, so a corrected quotation still reaches the triage (round 1's BLOCKED ruling, reversed).
decisions.why: Keeps under review an edit that changes what a page says a source says; it restricts the tool's clearing and narrows nothing the GM asked.

decisions.id: D4 the first filter's three arms
decisions.summary: change::fires sends a page's change on only where (1) a cited note key is gone, (2) the ECHO rule holds, or (3) a new bold-opened finding is added and the pop-up states a single case; a unit with no firing page is answered 'triage: cleared by the tool', no agent.
decisions.why: The GM approved 'the echo check as T186's first filter, the agent triage after it' (request.md, the narrowest check). Arms (1) and (3) only add to what reaches the agent beyond echo alone, and arm (1) keeps rule (C) reachable. Clearing a unit where nothing fires is the approved filter itself.

decisions.summary: The absence arm's phrases leave out 'not recorded' and 'no source' (the coordinator's wording) and keep 'the one case', 'only one case', 'every plan': 56 of 114 pop-ups fire instead of 104, 0 of 17 page-caused corrections missed either way (measured 2026-11-23, the landing replay and score).
decisions.why: The plan calls this a narrowing of the COORDINATOR's wording; that brief is neither the GM's request nor the accepted spec: a grep of request.md, spec-cited.md and spec-index.md for 'not recorded|no source|absence' finds no hit. The GM's words name only the echo check as the first filter, and the absence arm is an addition to it, so trimming the addition narrows nothing he asked. Purpose check: with the two phrases the arm fires on 104 of 114 pop-ups, which would gut the filter the GM approved to end needless cascades; the trimmed form shows no measured miss among the 17 page-caused corrections (the knob is chosen and scored on the same 17, as the green exit and the red exit in the section state).

decisions.summary: The triage MANIFEST shows each changed block OLD, NEW and WORD DIFF, the new and removed blocks, and each pop-up whole once (never cut at 400 characters).
decisions.why: Presentation for the approved agent triage after the filter; showing more, never less.

decisions.summary: modal-triage.md states (A) a fact the pop-up states, (B) a label of one, (C) a passage its references point at removed; the code states none of it; (D) is dropped.
decisions.why: The GM approved the plan in which 'the gap-fill clause [is] dropped' (request.md, the narrowest check); the section names this drop as (D), the GM's later form. Stating the rule in one place adds nothing and removes nothing.

decisions.summary: The rule to name a pop-up when unsure whether a block meets (A)-(C) is kept in modal-triage.md.
decisions.why: Round 2 ruled its drop NOT LEGITIMATE because the GM's approval dropped only the gap-fill clause; keeping it is the status quo that ruling required.

decisions.id: D9 notes and originals outside the fingerprint
decisions.summary: The section states .notes.html and .originals.html never reached a pop-up's checks (fingerprint reads only the Entry: and Drawing: pages), pinned by the replay's first class.
decisions.why: Describes and pins existing behavior; it changes no reach of review.

decisions.summary: record modal-triage replay --edits and --landing, the latter calling the same change::fires.
decisions.why: Verification that the approved filter does what it says (misses no page-caused correction); enforcement of the request, not scope.

decisions.summary: Before T185; T187 waits for the garden fix; green is the landing replay missing none of the 17 page-caused corrections; red narrows the arm that cleared a needed correction.
decisions.why: Sequencing and an exit that measures the GM's own criterion (catch every page-caused correction); nothing narrowed.

decisions.id: D12 comment label changes cleared, left
decisions.summary: An Evidence/Grounds comment's label change is cleared by the tool and was never re-owed on HEAD; not a defect, since each page states the label in visible words the triage sees; T187 (labels are data) is the label rule.
decisions.why: The GM's label question ('should attested versus guess be something that cascades mechanically rather than requiring a review') is answered by the approved rule 'labels are data and propagate by regeneration', carried by T187 by name. T186 leaves HEAD's behavior on comments as it was, the visible label is still reviewed, and no wrong outcome is left.

decisions.id: D13 claims triage not given T186's clears
decisions.summary: The claims triage gets T185's moves but not T186's tool clears and pairing; its agent still sees every changed block; said in the report.
decisions.why: Scope: the cascade the GM described is a page edit re-owing checks on every pop-up citing it, and his approval for this task names T186's filter on pop-up triage. The claims triage left as it is gives correct outcomes (its agent sees every changed block); a speed gap with correct outcomes is not a defect left (constitution XIV's defect rule), so nothing asked is given up here.

decisions.summary: The 'pond is taken as the office's form' sentence is restated in sheet/garden-pond.md, sheet/garden.md and docs/building-programs.md's inner_garden row (via make building-programs), to a garden's water being a knob; modal-form and modal-research owed on the two pop-ups through make record-owed.
decisions.why: The GM approved 'the garden-pond sentence fixed in its three places'; these are the three. Owing the two pop-ups' own checks directly adds review.

decisions.summary: A label becomes data on the page: an empty <span class=item data-item data-label data-guess> inside the item's block (not on its <li>, which style.rs and triage/change.rs match bare), the block's own words held to the tag by items::faults.
decisions.why: This is the GM's approved rule 'labels are data and propagate by regeneration', answering 'Shouldn't attested versus guess be something that cascades mechanically rather than requiring a review'. Where the span sits and the fact that it is empty are design choices inside that rule, and items::faults enforces it.

decisions.summary: A pop-up's Guesses bullet becomes a reference {NNNN#<id>} that the build fills from the tag and drops while the item is not a GUESS, hooked into about::feature and choices::modal so the page writer, registry dump, Mode A and the modal bundle all read the filled text.
decisions.why: This is the propagation by regeneration the GM approved. A relabel is one edit on the page, and the pop-ups follow it with no review.

decisions.summary: An engine claim may name ...html#<id>, and its class is checked against the tag. For such a claim alone the fingerprint leaves out the class word and the anchors, so a relabel flip owes no impl-drift. An unanchored claim keeps its class in its fingerprint. label_free stops the stale-figure check from reading the flip as a changed constant.
decisions.why: Claims are hand-written comments, so they are checked and told which class to write rather than regenerated. The cascade stays mechanical and owes no review, which is the purpose of the GM's question. The fingerprint exemption reaches only the case the request names, a claim held to a tag. label_free fixes, red first, a false flag the pilot found (TREE_ROOM).

decisions.summary: A registry real-tree test names any pop-up whose About states a GUESS-tagged item of a page it cites without calling it a guess.
decisions.why: Prose in an About section cannot be regenerated, so this test makes sure a label reaches the place regeneration does not. It only fails when the requested label cascade is missing, so it enforces the request and adds no new behavior (GM 2026-09-20).

decisions.summary: Tooling plus a pilot on page 0218, sheet/compound-shrine.md and the 4 shrine-tree claims. The remaining untagged record keeps the old review path, and T192 tags it.
decisions.why: This sequences the approved rule across tasks of the same feature and drops nothing: the bulk tagging is filed as T192. Nothing is wrongly cleared in the meantime, because an untagged item is treated as unknown and keeps the review it owes today (constitution XII).

decisions.summary: The 4 shrine-tree claims that cited 0218 as attested are restated as GUESS ...#shrine-tree. The code and the drawing are unchanged.
decisions.why: The label was wrong and the behavior was fine, so the claim is restated, as constitution XIV v2.36.0 directs. This is the uncascaded label the GM asked about, found and fixed.

decisions.summary: docs/building-programs.md's 'shrine in a corner beside a tree' cites 0218 as attested for a GUESS. The fix goes to T192, which lands before T22, because T186's uncommitted edit of that file is in this clone.
decisions.why: The defect is not dropped. It is filed, with a reason and an order (FR-009's form), and it is fixed inside this feature before T22. The GM's fix-as-we-go rule bounds known defects by the next step ('fix all known bugs in each step before moving on to porting the next step'), not by the task that found them. Keeping a hunk out of another builder's uncommitted file is about the order of landings and does not narrow the request.

decisions.summary: Lands after T186 (the triage's first filter, which clears a referenced relabel) and T185 (whose modal.rs this task edits in guesses() only), and before T192.
decisions.why: Sequencing. Nothing the request asks for is narrowed.

decisions.summary: T188/T189/T190: measure first (the replay over the clone's check state, replies and event logs) before the rules
decisions.why: Measurement before a rule is how the GM asked for this work to go (the convergence talk opens 'let's talk about that before we do literally anything else'). The replay's arithmetic holds (115+103+499+829=1546; 35+34+31+11+2+2=115; 17+8=25; 115-31=84), and it is labeled as a floor with its date and method.

decisions.summary: T188: the category rule applies per EDIT, not per reply. In a mixed round the wording EDITs (and GLOSSARY) go first, fingerprints are read (mid), then the factual ones. Only a unit that wording alone moved settles
decisions.why: This carries 'only factual findings cascade' as stated: a unit that a factual EDIT moved still re-owes. A per-reply rule would either skip factual changes or re-owe wording, and both would break the GM's rule.

decisions.summary: T188: an EDIT whose check or category is not given is factual, and a reply naming no check settles as before
decisions.why: A fail-safe default: a mislabel costs a round and never skips a factual review, which keeps what the GM's rule protects (factual inaccuracies still cascade).

decisions.summary: T188: the wording classes (never re-owe): modal-form, record-format (VOCABULARY, SESSION NOTE, HISTORY), record-style, intro-check
decisions.why: These are the GM's 'style edits are just a different category of thing than factual inaccuracies'. modal-form's contract already says a replacement only rewords, and the others are presentation or the order of words. A claim that one of them changes is not part of this table: it is factual by the untold/factual side, and each check's own contract binds it.

decisions.summary: T188: a modal-depiction LINKS EDIT (a pointer to a drawing page) is wording and does not cascade
decisions.why: Judged on its own, apart from the style checks. The GM's own words on splits cover it: 'as long as the original page being linked to directs a reader to the other page ... nothing needs to cascade'. A pointer to a drawing states no fact. What a statement rests on (REFERENCES) and what a drawing shows (COVERAGE, TRUTH) stay factual, so the seam is drawn on the fact line.

decisions.summary: T188: factual (may cascade): modal-research ACCURACY/REFERENCES/GAPS, modal-depiction COVERAGE/TRUTH, quote-check, source-reader, translation-check, entry-drift
decisions.why: These are the 'factual inaccuracies' the GM said cascading is for. Putting GAPS (a statement added) on the factual side is conservative.

decisions.summary: T188: quote-check's units stay on settle_quotes, which re-owes a unit whose quoted words changed, whoever changed them (a wording EDIT included)
decisions.why: A wording EDIT can still re-owe quote-check here, so this is a carve-out from 'wording never re-owes'. It is implied by the GM's own approved sibling rule 'only a claim-changing edit triggers review': changed quoted words change the claim about what a source says, which is a factual matter. A unit whose quoted words and claim held is already settled, so the GM's purpose (no rounds that fix nothing) is kept.

decisions.summary: T188: no change for building-review (error/questionable/nitpick/outside) or impl-drift (IN-STEP/DRIFTED/MISLABELED)
decisions.why: Taken one check at a time. Neither applies EDITs through make apply-edits. building-review is re-owed by the sheet's own fingerprint, and impl-drift by the code's and claims' fingerprints. A record or pop-up wording EDIT, the cascade the GM described ('a page edit re-owes checks on every pop-up citing it'), moves neither fingerprint, so the rule has nothing there to act on. The plan does not narrow the rule here: the cascade it targets does not pass through these checks.

decisions.summary: T188: only modal-depiction's contract gains a category in its EDIT header; every other check is one class throughout
decisions.why: This is the mechanism for telling modal-depiction's mixed classes apart. For every other check, the check's name already says its class.

decisions.summary: T189: a later round's bundle gains 'The change since round <n>', which pairs every changed run of lines since what the last round was bundled (EDITs and hand edits alike). The instruction is to judge only whether the change made something wrong, and the whole unit stays for context
decisions.why: This is 're-reviews scoped to the change'. Including hand edits makes the pairing complete rather than narrow. The scope reaches the reviewer as an instruction: what a reviewer judges cannot be enforced mechanically, and the 11-19 'real enforcement' approval was about the six improvements' guards. The mechanical part, the paired change in the bundle, is built.

decisions.summary: T189: a subject whose last round was bundled before the keeping gets no change section and reads the whole unit unscoped, as before
decisions.why: A transitional carve-out from 'scoped to the change'. What such a round was handed was never kept (the plan's premise: the bundle is overwritten on regeneration, and uncommitted EDITs and hand edits are not in git), so 'every change since the last round' cannot be paired for it. Telling a reviewer to judge ONLY a pairing that might miss a change would let an unpaired claim change through unreviewed, which defeats the GM's sibling rule 'only a claim-changing edit triggers review'. The carve-out ends by itself: that round writes the kept bundle, so each subject is scoped from its next round on.

decisions.summary: T190: apply_edits/settled.rs refuses, before applying anything, an EDIT whose new text is an earlier round's EDIT's old text and whose old text is that EDIT's new text
decisions.why: This is 'settled choices stay settled' for the review rounds' oscillation that the GM raised under 'On oscillation and review scope'. It is a real refusal with a red-first test (the refusal off: failed).

decisions.summary: T190: the refusal uses the exact put-back test; the looser near_reversal (two content words back) stays a mark
decisions.why: Measured on 2026-11-23 over 1,670 EDITs: 3 were exact put-backs, and the loose test named 17 more that read as factual rounds widening a sentence. Refusing on the loose test would block factual corrections, which defeats the purpose the GM gave ('we are only interested in factual inaccuracies'). The near cases remain visible as marks.

decisions.summary: T190: a put-back is let through only when its finding carries 'REVERSES round <n>:' and an 'evidence:' quoting the words or naming the page, and its check's category is factual. A wording put-back has no way through
decisions.why: An exception to 'settled choices stay settled', taken on its own. Refusing every put-back of a settled fact would lock in a factual error that an earlier round introduced, which defeats the GM's stated purpose (fixing real flaws, factual inaccuracies). Requiring the stated error and its evidence keeps settled wording settled and allows no escape for style. FR-012's escape requirement covers the refusals of FR-006 to FR-009, FR-011 and FR-013, not this one, so leaving wording without an escape conflicts with no requirement.

decisions.summary: T190 (found and left): no refusal on the Edit tool for hand put-backs
decisions.why: Judged on the replay alone, case by case, not on the cited reversal:<file> rulings, which the bundle does not carry. In 24 of the 25 measured Edit-tool A->B->A put-backs a builder was revising its own code with no round between: nothing was settled. In the 1 (no_poll_hooks.rs) spec-fidelity replies came between, but no check's EDIT was involved: a spec review settles no code wording. The GM's rule sits under 'oscillation and review scope', that is, rounds undoing rounds, and that is refused at apply-edits. A hand edit of a record page is not a round's choice, and T189 still hands it to the next round as a paired change to judge.

decisions.summary: T188/T189/T190: filed as [perf] tasks; the saving is stated as a floor of 84 of 115 wording-only later rounds, and the rest is a GUESS to be measured after landing
decisions.why: FR-013 counts the builders' loop and review rounds as performance work. The figures carry their date and method, and the unmeasured part is labeled GUESS.

blocks: ### T186 (the GM 2026-11-23, request.md 'the convergence talk': "I want to figure out what the difference is between the ones that might plausibly have required that and the ones that were just straightforward adjustments that never could have plausibly needed this kind of cascade"; the blind re-classification, reclassify.md)

decisions.summary: Footnote markers and markup are taken out of a block's claim words. A block whose claim words are unchanged, or empty, is cleared by the tool with no agent.
decisions.why: This carries the GM's approved rule 'only a claim-changing edit triggers review' and his question about edits 'that never could have plausibly needed this kind of cascade'. A marker or markup edit leaves every claim word the same. A key that goes away is still caught by arm (1).

decisions.summary: Original-language quotations are NOT taken out of claim words. Round 1's BLOCKED finding is honored and the stripping is removed from the code.
decisions.why: This sends more edits on than the round-1 form did. A corrected quotation changes what a page says a source says, so it stays a claim change. It narrows nothing that was asked.

decisions.summary: Old and new blocks are paired: exact matches first, then the tool's clears, then pairs at difflib ratio 0.6 or more.
decisions.why: This is how the change is computed. It decides nothing the request or spec states, and unpaired blocks still reach the triage as new or removed.

decisions.summary: change::fires is the first filter. A pop-up is owed triage only on (1) a Sources key gone, (2) the ECHO rule, or (3) a new bold-opened finding plus a pop-up that states a single case. A unit where no page fires is cleared by the tool, its pages kept.
decisions.why: The GM approved 'the echo check as T186's first filter, the agent triage after it'. Arms (1) and (3) only add to what the echo sends on. The landing replay measured 0 of the 17 page-caused corrections missed (one-shot label, 2026-11-23, replay --landing on both commits, scored against needed.md).

decisions.summary: ABSENCE is narrowed from the coordinator's five phrases to three. 'not recorded' and 'no source' are dropped: 104 of 114 fire with them, 56 of 114 without, 0 of 17 missed either way.
decisions.why: The longer phrase list came from the coordinator's brief, not from the GM's request or the accepted spec. request.md asks only for the echo check first and the agent after, and has no absence arm. Narrowing a session-added arm narrows nothing the GM asked for. The choice is measured, with 0 of 17 missed at each setting, and the knob is labeled as one.

decisions.summary: The triage MANIFEST shows each changed block as OLD, NEW and a word diff, the new and removed blocks, and each pop-up whole once, never cut at 400 characters.
decisions.why: This shows the agent the change and the claims it may affect, so it can judge whether a claim changed. It only adds information.

decisions.summary: modal-triage.md states the contract once as (A) a fact the pop-up states, (B) a label of one, (C) a passage its references point at removed. (D) is dropped.
decisions.why: The GM approved 'the gap-fill clause dropped'. (A)-(C) match his approved rules: only a claim-changing edit triggers review, labels are data, and only factual findings cascade.

decisions.summary: The old triage contract's rule to name a pop-up when unsure is dropped.
decisions.why: The GM's own words already imply this. His approved rules are 'only a claim-changing edit triggers review' and 'only factual findings cascade', and he asked that edits that 'never could have plausibly needed this kind of cascade' not cascade. A default that sends on whatever the agent cannot place is what produced the cascade he asked to end: bundle 2's triage sent 79 of 114 on. Under (A)-(C) the agent still has to judge every pop-up the filter sends. The section says plainly that the contract has not been run on these bundles.

decisions.summary: .notes.html and .originals.html never reached a pop-up's checks, because the fingerprint reads only the Entry and Drawing pages. This is pinned by the replay's first class.
decisions.why: This records and pins existing behavior. A test that pins it serves the request.

decisions.summary: Two verbs: replay --edits replays the tool's clears over recorded edits, and replay --landing replays the whole live filter over a landed commit's edits.
decisions.why: Both check that the filter clears without missing a needed correction. This is enforcement of what was asked, not unrequested scope.

### T187 Performance checklist (docs/performance-checklist.md - prompts, never a gate; time is the goal, calls the measure)

decisions.summary: A label becomes data on the page: an empty <span class=item data-item data-label data-guess> inside the item's block (not on its <li>, which style.rs and triage/change.rs match bare), the block's own words held to the tag by items::faults.
decisions.why: This is the GM's approved rule 'labels are data and propagate by regeneration', answering 'Shouldn't attested versus guess be something that cascades mechanically rather than requiring a review'. Where the span sits and the fact that it is empty are design choices inside that rule, and items::faults enforces it.

decisions.summary: A pop-up's Guesses bullet becomes a reference {NNNN#<id>} that the build fills from the tag and drops while the item is not a GUESS, hooked into about::feature and choices::modal so the page writer, registry dump, Mode A and the modal bundle all read the filled text.
decisions.why: This is the propagation by regeneration the GM approved. A relabel is one edit on the page, and the pop-ups follow it with no review.

decisions.summary: An engine claim may name ...html#<id>, and its class is checked against the tag. For such a claim alone the fingerprint leaves out the class word and the anchors, so a relabel flip owes no impl-drift. An unanchored claim keeps its class in its fingerprint. label_free stops the stale-figure check from reading the flip as a changed constant.
decisions.why: Claims are hand-written comments, so they are checked and told which class to write rather than regenerated. The cascade stays mechanical and owes no review, which is the purpose of the GM's question. The fingerprint exemption reaches only the case the request names, a claim held to a tag. label_free fixes, red first, a false flag the pilot found (TREE_ROOM).

decisions.summary: A registry real-tree test names any pop-up whose About states a GUESS-tagged item of a page it cites without calling it a guess.
decisions.why: Prose in an About section cannot be regenerated, so this test makes sure a label reaches the place regeneration does not. It only fails when the requested label cascade is missing, so it enforces the request and adds no new behavior (GM 2026-09-20).

### T188, T189, T190 Approach (checklist part A)
### T188, T189, T190 Performance checklist (docs/performance-checklist.md - prompts, never a gate; time is the goal, calls the measure)

decisions.summary: T188/T189/T190: measure first (the replay over the clone's check state, replies and event logs) before the rules
decisions.why: Measurement before a rule is how the GM asked for this work to go (the convergence talk opens 'let's talk about that before we do literally anything else'). The replay's arithmetic holds (115+103+499+829=1546; 35+34+31+11+2+2=115; 17+8=25; 115-31=84), and it is labeled as a floor with its date and method.

decisions.summary: T188: the category rule applies per EDIT, not per reply. In a mixed round the wording EDITs (and GLOSSARY) go first, fingerprints are read (mid), then the factual ones. Only a unit that wording alone moved settles
decisions.why: This carries 'only factual findings cascade' as stated: a unit that a factual EDIT moved still re-owes. A per-reply rule would either skip factual changes or re-owe wording, and both would break the GM's rule.

decisions.summary: T188: an EDIT whose check or category is not given is factual, and a reply naming no check settles as before
decisions.why: A fail-safe default: a mislabel costs a round and never skips a factual review, which keeps what the GM's rule protects (factual inaccuracies still cascade).

decisions.summary: T188: the wording classes (never re-owe): modal-form, record-format (VOCABULARY, SESSION NOTE, HISTORY), record-style, intro-check
decisions.why: These are the GM's 'style edits are just a different category of thing than factual inaccuracies'. modal-form's contract already says a replacement only rewords, and the others are presentation or the order of words. A claim that one of them changes is not part of this table: it is factual by the untold/factual side, and each check's own contract binds it.

decisions.summary: T188: a modal-depiction LINKS EDIT (a pointer to a drawing page) is wording and does not cascade
decisions.why: Judged on its own, apart from the style checks. The GM's own words on splits cover it: 'as long as the original page being linked to directs a reader to the other page ... nothing needs to cascade'. A pointer to a drawing states no fact. What a statement rests on (REFERENCES) and what a drawing shows (COVERAGE, TRUTH) stay factual, so the seam is drawn on the fact line.

decisions.summary: T188: factual (may cascade): modal-research ACCURACY/REFERENCES/GAPS, modal-depiction COVERAGE/TRUTH, quote-check, source-reader, translation-check, entry-drift
decisions.why: These are the 'factual inaccuracies' the GM said cascading is for. Putting GAPS (a statement added) on the factual side is conservative.

decisions.summary: T188: quote-check's units stay on settle_quotes, which re-owes a unit whose quoted words changed, whoever changed them (a wording EDIT included)
decisions.why: A wording EDIT can still re-owe quote-check here, so this is a carve-out from 'wording never re-owes'. It is implied by the GM's own approved sibling rule 'only a claim-changing edit triggers review': changed quoted words change the claim about what a source says, which is a factual matter. A unit whose quoted words and claim held is already settled, so the GM's purpose (no rounds that fix nothing) is kept.

decisions.summary: T188: no change for building-review (error/questionable/nitpick/outside) or impl-drift (IN-STEP/DRIFTED/MISLABELED)
decisions.why: Taken one check at a time. Neither applies EDITs through make apply-edits. building-review is re-owed by the sheet's own fingerprint, and impl-drift by the code's and claims' fingerprints. A record or pop-up wording EDIT, the cascade the GM described ('a page edit re-owes checks on every pop-up citing it'), moves neither fingerprint, so the rule has nothing there to act on. The plan does not narrow the rule here: the cascade it targets does not pass through these checks.

decisions.summary: T188: only modal-depiction's contract gains a category in its EDIT header; every other check is one class throughout
decisions.why: This is the mechanism for telling modal-depiction's mixed classes apart. For every other check, the check's name already says its class.

decisions.summary: T189: a later round's bundle gains 'The change since round <n>', which pairs every changed run of lines since what the last round was bundled (EDITs and hand edits alike). The instruction is to judge only whether the change made something wrong, and the whole unit stays for context
decisions.why: This is 're-reviews scoped to the change'. Including hand edits makes the pairing complete rather than narrow. The scope reaches the reviewer as an instruction: what a reviewer judges cannot be enforced mechanically, and the 11-19 'real enforcement' approval was about the six improvements' guards. The mechanical part, the paired change in the bundle, is built.

decisions.summary: T189: a subject whose last round was bundled before the keeping gets no change section and reads the whole unit unscoped, as before
decisions.why: A transitional carve-out from 'scoped to the change'. What such a round was handed was never kept (the plan's premise: the bundle is overwritten on regeneration, and uncommitted EDITs and hand edits are not in git), so 'every change since the last round' cannot be paired for it. Telling a reviewer to judge ONLY a pairing that might miss a change would let an unpaired claim change through unreviewed, which defeats the GM's sibling rule 'only a claim-changing edit triggers review'. The carve-out ends by itself: that round writes the kept bundle, so each subject is scoped from its next round on.

decisions.summary: T190: apply_edits/settled.rs refuses, before applying anything, an EDIT whose new text is an earlier round's EDIT's old text and whose old text is that EDIT's new text
decisions.why: This is 'settled choices stay settled' for the review rounds' oscillation that the GM raised under 'On oscillation and review scope'. It is a real refusal with a red-first test (the refusal off: failed).

decisions.summary: T190: the refusal uses the exact put-back test; the looser near_reversal (two content words back) stays a mark
decisions.why: Measured on 2026-11-23 over 1,670 EDITs: 3 were exact put-backs, and the loose test named 17 more that read as factual rounds widening a sentence. Refusing on the loose test would block factual corrections, which defeats the purpose the GM gave ('we are only interested in factual inaccuracies'). The near cases remain visible as marks.

decisions.summary: T190: a put-back is let through only when its finding carries 'REVERSES round <n>:' and an 'evidence:' quoting the words or naming the page, and its check's category is factual. A wording put-back has no way through
decisions.why: An exception to 'settled choices stay settled', taken on its own. Refusing every put-back of a settled fact would lock in a factual error that an earlier round introduced, which defeats the GM's stated purpose (fixing real flaws, factual inaccuracies). Requiring the stated error and its evidence keeps settled wording settled and allows no escape for style. FR-012's escape requirement covers the refusals of FR-006 to FR-009, FR-011 and FR-013, not this one, so leaving wording without an escape conflicts with no requirement.

decisions.summary: T190 (found and left): no refusal on the Edit tool for hand put-backs
decisions.why: Judged on the replay alone, case by case, not on the cited reversal:<file> rulings, which the bundle does not carry. In 24 of the 25 measured Edit-tool A->B->A put-backs a builder was revising its own code with no round between: nothing was settled. In the 1 (no_poll_hooks.rs) spec-fidelity replies came between, but no check's EDIT was involved: a spec review settles no code wording. The GM's rule sits under 'oscillation and review scope', that is, rounds undoing rounds, and that is refused at apply-edits. A hand edit of a record page is not a round's choice, and T189 still hands it to the next round as a paired change to judge.

decisions.summary: T188/T189/T190: filed as [perf] tasks; the saving is stated as a floor of 84 of 115 wording-only later rounds, and the rest is a GUESS to be measured after landing
decisions.why: FR-013 counts the builders' loop and review rounds as performance work. The figures carry their date and method, and the unmeasured part is labeled GUESS.
